hero.title: Captain Aaron G. Lane
hero.subtitle: Piermont farmer, Mexican War veteran, Forty-niner — first permanent settler on the Mojave River at Lane's Crossing on the Mormon Road.
hero.portraitCaption: Exhibit portrait — Lane Museum card and major-achievers roster.

kinship.summary: Aaron G. Lane is Homer Lane's first cousin, three times removed (Vol. I). Twin brother Moses P. Lane died at Acapulco en route to California; Moses's daughter Eldora Richmond nursed Aaron at Halleck in 1883.

familyThread.title: Moses Lane & the Richmonds
familyThread.lede: Vol. I ties Aaron's late life to his twin's line — Moses never reached California; Eldora closed the story at Halleck.

entries.name: Moses P. Lane
entries.note: Died 21 June 1852 at Acapulco, Mexico, on his way to California — probably to join Aaron.

entries.name: Eldora (Mrs. George) Richmond
entries.note: Moses's daughter; Aaron's home was in her household at Halleck. She nursed him in 1882–83.

familyThread.caution: Eldora's person node may be incomplete in the graph — relationship is book-clear; graph links need review.

evidence.label: Lane Genealogies Vol. I (1891), p. 148
evidence.body: CAPT. AARON G.⁶ (twin brother to Moses), b. 23 Dec., 1817, went to California in 1849, and was widely known in the early history of the state. He died unm. 14 Sept., 1883, at Lane's Crossing of the Mojave river. His home was in the family of Mrs. Richmond, his neice, in Halleck, Cal.

evidence.label: Mojave corridor & routes
evidence.body: Lane's Crossing was the Last Crossing of the Mojave on the Mormon Road — travelers left the river here for Cajon Pass. Thompson's Pioneer of the Mojave, Wikipedia, USC/LOC photos, and HMDB markers extend the book line.

timeline.title: Born Piermont, N.H.
timeline.body: Youngest son of Jonathan Lane and Mary Towle; twin to Moses P. Lane.

timeline.title: Mexico & malaria
timeline.body: Co. H, 9th U.S. Infantry; invalid pension 1849 after fever at Puebla.

timeline.title: Forty-niner
timeline.body: Panama crossing; Mother Lode ventures; then San Bernardino.

timeline.title: Lane's Crossing
timeline.body: Ranch and store at Lower Narrows — first settlement on the Mojave River.

timeline.title: Bryman ranch
timeline.body: Alfalfa, Camp Cady provisioning, civic offices; sold the crossing.

timeline.title: Died at Bryman
timeline.body: 14 Sept.; nursed by niece Eldora Richmond at Halleck.

places.title: Map — New Hampshire to the Mojave
places.lede: Select a moment on the right — the map flies to that stop. Pins trace Aaron's arc from Piermont to Lane's Crossing and Bryman.

items.name: Piermont, N.H.
items.note: Peaked Mountain farm; NH militia with twin Moses. Departure for Mexico and California.

items.name: Puebla, Mexico
items.note: 9th Infantry march; malaria during siege — shaped his move west.

items.name: Mother Lode, Calif.
items.note: Gold Rush diggings before San Bernardino and the desert corridor.

items.name: Lane's Crossing
items.note: Lower Narrows ford — Last Crossing of the Mojave. Turner Ranch / Victorville today.

items.name: Bryman / Halleck
items.note: Downriver alfalfa ranch; niece Eldora Richmond; death 14 Sept. 1883.

routes.title: Western settlement routes
beats: Mohave Trail — indigenous trade route at Lower Narrows (Serrano-Vanyume village Tobiabit).
Old Spanish Trail (1830s) — New Mexico to Alta California; western arm crossed below the narrows.
Mormon Road — Salt Lake to Los Angeles; Last Crossing before Cajon Pass.
Mojave Road (1858+) — Prescott AZ to Wilmington CA through Lane's station.
